utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances today, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. For Mico Stanisic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Tatjana Savic, and Eugene O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Aleksandar Aleksic for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. While the witness is on his way in, I understand that there are no preliminary matters, but the Chamber wishes to confirm - and this, we think, would have already been communicated to Mr. Cvijetic - that we must take the break at 10.00 because the three of us are involved in a meeting. At that time we will reconvene at 10.30 and rise for the day at 11.15, so that if, heaven forbid, the witness, Mr. Cvijetic, is not finished at that time, then the rest of his -- the remainder of his cross-examination will have to abide the return next week.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think you meant re-examination, Your Honour. I really have finished cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. Yes, re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, good morning to you. Before I invite Mr. Cvijetic to begin his re-examination, I give you the usual reminder about your solemn declaration. Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask the Usher to give our binder to the witness, in case we need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Orasanin.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, during cross-examination by Ms. Korner regarding information in the Ilijas and Vogosca SJBs, and that's P989 for your reference, in this report you said that communications were down - that's on the last page of this report - and that's communications between the Vogosca and Ilijas SJBs, even though they were quite close, geographically. Ms. Korner showed you a document that was a bulletin of daily events, and it was marked as Exhibit P1437. I would like to have this exhibit on the screens for a moment, please. In paragraph 2, you were told that there is a report of events from Vogosca municipality and from the front in Ilijas, and this contests your claim that communications were down. Mr. Milanovic -- Orasanin, could this information in this bulletin have arrived from the Yugoslav People's Army as well? Please look at paragraph 1; which says -- please look at paragraph 1. So could this information have arrived from these organs? Only yes or no, because we don't have a lot of time.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My second question regarding this information: Could it have arrived personally? Could it have been given verbally by somebody who participated in combat, just as you once went and reported verbally?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I wanted to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You can't comment on it. Just tell me yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll say this once just: Re-examination doesn't mean you can ask leading questions. The proper way of asking the question, if you wanted to, is, Are you aware of any other method by which they could have got this information? Not by asking those sort of leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe these questions are not very leading, but I will try to adjust them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, when you were doing this visit, could you call the centre of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time. But there were two communications towards Vogosca which were safe at different times.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: No, but were you able to call them?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before we do that, could we have paragraph 4 on the screen? That is the next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Have you read paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Which begins with what, Mr. Cvijetic? Do you read the beginning of it in Serbian so that we see what it is about?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you referring to the paragraph that goes: "The Serbian forces are successfully advancing while fighting in down-town Sarajevo"? Is that the paragraph you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If that's the paragraph you showed the witness, that's okay. We've seen it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not the one. It was paragraph 1, paragraph 1 that mentions the Yugoslav People's Army. That's why I asked him whether they could have got that information through the Yugoslav People's Army. And then the second paragraph related to Vogosca that he visited. Then paragraph 3 mentions Ilijas, which he also visited. So it was paragraphs 1, 2 and 3, Your Honours. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Cvijetic, my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, here you talked about the communications system, and I would like to know whether you knew that there was an instruction on the urgent and current information being provided in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was such an information to report urgently and on time. That was taken over from the previous times.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please just answer yes or no, because we don't have a lot of time. That's why I'm trying to get you to hurry up. Did you need an appropriate communications system for such reporting? Can you please just tell me whether you needed a communications system in order to meet this obligation of informing?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well, you've answered my question. When did that communications system start functioning in 1992? In your opinion, when did it start functioning in the entire territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, it was in late 1992. I was talking about official communications, cryptographic data protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now listen to this: This system of reporting, after the system was established in all of Republika Srpska, or beforehand, in those areas where some communications existed, were local public security stations able to send information that you later established, after you arrived in the field, that they weren't realistic? Were there any such situations?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Reports weren't arriving. You could send reports in person, by courier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You didn't understand my question. The question was clear. During your visits, did you establish that the situation in the field was different to what you thought before you had set out?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I talked about that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. That's what I'm asking you. My next question: As far as your visits and instructive inspections are concerned, among others, were they also to inform the Ministry of the Interior about what was happening in the field?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You put these visits into two categories: There were blitz visits, as you call them, and there were instructive inspections.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Which is the best way for the ministry to get accurate information about what was happening in the field, of all of the types that we've mentioned now?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only based on instructive inspections, which were based on the instructions for such inspections of the SJBs, if a high-quality instructive inspection was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go back to your visits and instructive inspections. Now I'll move on to the next topic. During cross-examination, you were shown a document that was a payroll from the Ministry of the Interior at the centre. Do you recall this document?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the reference, I'll say it's 1D569. Could we please have that on the screen. I would like to ask the witness some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The tab number, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's tab 3 in the Defence binder. And to be honest, I can't find it in the Prosecution binder, but I believe Ms. Korner used it as well. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, I would just like to illustrate something with this. Tell me, please, when did you practically start working in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Just shortly. When did you start working?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In early May, on the 4th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Hold on, I'll ask you. And when were you appointed?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was appointed on the 6th of May; not only I, but quite a few other employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let us correct this in the record. Could you please tell us when you were appointed, because the transcript says something else?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Could you please just answer my question, and don't rush until I'm finished with my question. Now I would like to know why this was done.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most cases, this was done just to link up years of service. The salary was so low, so insignificant, but the entitlement to retirement and to years of pensionable service was significant, and so this employment of the first one to three months was linked up in order to be entitled to years of pensionable service.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. That was the essence of my question. My next question is this: Then the payroll of the employees in the centre and in public security stations, did they show realistically the number of employees in the first two or three months, as employees were still arriving? Please just answer me.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not realistic indicators, because this is a separate service.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I just want to know whether they're realistic or not.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well, we're done with that question. I will not use Ms. Korner's methods and say that you won't go home tomorrow if you don't answer quickly, but --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know quite a lot of employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether this was done in the MUP at the centre, at the CSBs and at the SJBs, that years of pensionable service were linked up? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well, you've answered my question. Let's move on. You were shown a payroll list for the Skelani SJB, so I would like to have Exhibit 8D1 on the screen. You don't have it there. It's a Prosecution exhibit. Please take a look at the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was tab 18 in the Prosecution binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at that list. Oh, it's not on the screen yet. This is 65 ter 8D1. It's still not the one. I apologise, Your Honours. No, I gave you the wrong number. It's 65 ter 20163. It's earlier tab 16A in the Prosecution binder. I apologise. There we go. Can you see it? We'll just wait. Mr. Orasanin, when discussing this list, on transcript pages of the 8th of June, and these are pages 22064, 22065 and 22066, you were told that during your testimony you said that while visiting Skelani, you only saw Mr. Milanovic, and that you had the impression that this station wasn't functioning. And then you were shown this document, and you were asked whether this document actually showed that in this small town, in May, there was, indeed, a police station that worked with 10 policemen, and you replied: "Yes, this list proves that." Do you remember replying that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it functioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you merely whether you remember the answer that you gave, and then I'm going to ask you something else about it. So do you remember or do you not remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Ms. Korner then said, at 22065, that this shows that the Public Security Station -- that Skelani had a proper public security station. Later on, you spoke about this commentary of hers. After it had been concluded that you gave a wrong impression to the Trial Chamber, when you said that there was nobody in Skelani during your visit, later, on 22066, it was said that this was a fully functional station that had a commander, a chief, and eight working policemen. Do you remember that that's what Ms. Korner said, that that was a fully functional police station? This is what it says in our transcript. Mr. Orasanin, this list, is it a sufficient and reliable proof that the policemen listed here actually worked during the time when you were visiting there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a payroll. The situation in the field was not like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right, all right. Let me ask you another question. What is the proper way --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I actually -- I'll leave aside the summary and the propriety of trying to contradict your own witness, but I applied to make this an exhibit and Your Honours said, no, because it was outside the area. But in the light of the fact that it's been gone back over in re-examination, I think it would probably be more helpful if it could now be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Do you have a view on that, Mr. Cvijetic? You're using it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document was presented here, accompanied by a claim that it establishes the lack of credibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I know the argument -- [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I want to establish that his statements about the work of this station and the number of employees in the station were accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner is asking that this document now be exhibited because you're using it again in redirect. What is your position on that? Do you agree or do you object?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that it was admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. It was my conviction that this was shown to the witness and admitted. So this is related to Skelani, and that's why we concluded that this municipality is not covered by the indictment, and that's why it actually wasn't admitted, but it was used for this other particular limited purpose, and I'm also using it for this other purpose. I simply want to establish whether the witness spoke the truth or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Let me ask you again. Can we admit it or do you object?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't want it to be admitted. I'm using it merely to illustrate a topic that I'm currently discussing with the witness, and that's the issue of his credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2354, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, can we conclude from this document whether the police station functioned properly in all its elements? Is it possible to arrive at such a conclusion based on this document alone?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Then I'm going to show you another document, P993. It's tab 40. I think it's a Prosecution document. Mr. Orasanin --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: -- when you said that that payroll was not sufficient, could you now tell me: What is a proper way to establish whether a police station is functioning?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only through instructive inspection. That is the only way stipulated by the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you take a look at this report on the supervisory inspection, among other stations, in Skelani police station as well. Is that the document?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait, wait. Can we have the last page so that the witness could see who signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you know who the signature is?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's Drago Borovcanin. He was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 2 of this document. In Serbian - let me count the paragraphs - the fifth paragraph, beginning with the words: "So far, this public security station has not achieved any significant results in its work." Take a look at that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The following paragraph, Mr. Borovcanin finds that there was a dual appointment of the key executives. Two were appointed by the MUP, and another two were appointed by the local authorities. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that that was the actual situation at some point? Did Mr. Borovcanin tell you about it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, I know that there were problems. I was in charge of border police, and I knew about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the last paragraph, where it says -- wait, listen to me. Of all the employees, only four were appointed?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following paragraph, please. It's on the next page in Serbian. It's the same page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Would you read the first paragraph in Serbian, and then I'm going to ask you a question. Can you see it, where it says: "It was not possible to organise --" Well, exactly, that's your purview, your service?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Then let us take a look at the last paragraph on this page. Yes, on the same page, the last paragraph. Read it, please. In English, it's the following page. So read the conclusions of Mr. Borovcanin. He says that there is no service that you were in charge, that there was no national security service, no judicial and other service, and that the problems are too dogged. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And he's of the opinion that the current personnel is not in the position to independently solve all these problems?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Take a look at his proposal: that a mixed working group consisting of officers from the department for fighting crime, and other departments, should be sent there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Continue listening to me. Can we have the last page in Serbian. At the very beginning of the page, Mr. Borovcanin proposes that if the working group assesses, a part of the special unit of the ministry should be sent there. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, the question: Was there a functioning public security station in Skelani?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's what we saw while we performed the first inspection. I already said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Does this report confirm your first impression that you conveyed to the Trial Chamber during the beginning of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The police station there did not function within the MUP Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. So much for Skelani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, did we or will we hear from the man who drafted this report, Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He already testified.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just hold on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me answer the Judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not quite clear on the status. Could we go into private session, and then Mr. - what's his name? - Cvijetic can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let us move to the questions that you were asked related to the situation in Zvornik. You were shown another payroll in relation to Zvornik. It was 65 ter 20159. Can we have it on the screens, please. Yes. We need to see the contents of the document. If this is the first page, then perhaps we should see the third page. Please read this document, Mr. Orasanin. You do not need to read it aloud. Mr. Orasanin, do you see the date in the upper left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have, just for a moment, the following page, and then we are going to back to the first page. So this is now the list of the employees that are listed on the payroll for the previous month. Now, can we have the first page again. Excuse me, I meant the page just before this one. Yes, this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, Milos Pantelic, the chief, requests the funds for the salaries for the month of May. My question is: The people listed here, were they and could they have been, objectively speaking, employed in the month of May, or can we arrive at this conclusion based on the payroll sheet? Is this a reliable proof?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This confirms what I said earlier, that they were not the members of the MUP of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the addressee.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's to the Serbian Temporary Municipal Government in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: At 20879, you said that the Public Security Station in Zvornik was covered by the overall MUP control only after the Yellow Wasps were eliminated, and then it was Djokanovic [as interpreted] who was appointed, after the position of the chief, and he was the first person appointed by the ministry. Do you remember that's what you told me?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let me just check the transcript. Not "Djokanovic." What was the name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lokancevic, Milorad.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: No. Tell us that once again slowly, loudly.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief was appointed by the MUP, and his name was Milorad Bokancevic [as interpreted]. It was sometime in mid-July.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Slowly. All right. The first letter is "L", Lokancevic, but we have the name in the documents. My question is: The document on the screen, does it confirm that the Public Security Station was controlled by the local authorities?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was all. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, but it has got top. Although Your Honours will take into account that what's on the transcript is adduced from leading questions, sometimes later it may be difficult to remember this. Mr. Cvijetic really cannot say to his own witness, Does it confirm that the Public Security Station was controlled by the local authorities, particularly when that whole matter of the relationship between the police and the crisis staffs is a subject which is at issue between the Prosecution and Defence. The questions must be asked in non-leading form. That is, what, where, how, where, when, is how the questions start, not by presenting a fact and asking the witness to confirm it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Of course, put another way, Mr. Cvijetic, what counsel for both sides are doing is highlighting certain documents with a view to, when we come to the stage of submissions, inviting the Chamber to draw certain inferences from those documents. So at this stage, having regard to the ground that has been covered, especially in cross-examination, I suppose the utility of this witness is really highlighting, for the benefit of the record, for the benefit of the Chamber, the relevant documents on which you would be relying to draw the inferences contrary to those invited by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will explain why I'm following this line of questioning. Well, first of all, I just reminded the witness of his own evidence, and he confirmed, so that should not be in contest. Now, on page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the transcript page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ... the witness spoke about the fact that the local stations were frequently under Crisis Staff control and local authorities. He said that when speaking about Zvornik, and I made a reference to that, so that I don't think my question was inappropriate. The second reason, Your Honours, why I'm dealing with this, is that when this evidence was adduced during cross-examination, it was done so in order to show that this witness is not reliable, when he described that his evidence was not reliable about the time when he described the situation at the Public Security Station in Karakaj. I just would like to intervene for the transcript. The page of transcript was 20049 [as interpreted], line 12. 22049, 22049, line 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, it remains for us -- and again this is to shed some light on the issue of your reliability, because that was questioned in reference to your evidence about Bijeljina. Now, in yesterday's transcript, page number -- just bear with me for a moment, please. Page 16, lines 1 and 2, in response to Ms. Korner's question, where she asked you to state clearly whether Mr. Jesuric, Predrag, at some point in time was the chief of the CSB in Bijeljina, to which you replied: "It is, of course, logical that he was a chief." And you explained why, and you made a reference to the competent courts. And you said that where there was a court seat, there were CSBs as well. Do you remember replying to that question in this manner?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Ms. Korner also put to you some provisions of the Law of Internal Affairs, which clearly showed that there were five centres of security services established in the republic. Do you remember that you were shown that part of the law?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We will not go into all the five of them, but one of them was the Bijeljina CSB; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now, we do not contest that Bijeljina had a CSB, and this is in reply to Ms. Korner's argument yesterday, and that Mr. Jesuric was the chief of that centre. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to show you the documents that led to some doubts about your reliability, and I would like to show you the first document that you were shown by Ms. Korner yesterday. That's P2352. P2352, please. Now, please take a look at this document, Mr. Orasanin. Could we just blow up the upper part of the document so that we can see the agency in question. That's in the left upper-hand corner. Can you see that the heading shows that this document was sent from the Public Security Station in Bijeljina? Can you see that part?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "Public Security Station, Bijeljina."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, please take a look below, where we see the signature and the stamp. Can we blow that portion up, please. Here, we clearly see that Mr. Jesuric signed this document as the chief of the CSB. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you also determine where this stamp comes from or who it belongs to?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says the Centre of the Security Services, Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Could you see the next line?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says "Public Security Station, Bijeljina." So both the heading and the stamp are those of the security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm just trying to point out why there was some confusion regarding your reliability and your answers. I would like to show you another document --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before we move on, I'm sorry, you can't mislead the Court. What the document says and what he's read out is it says, the "CSB and the SJB," and so does the stamp, apparently. It doesn't say just the "SJB Bijeljina."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps I should explain this. All public security stations have -- as part of their name, they have the "Centre of Security Services" -- well, let me put this question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, whose stamp is this that we see here?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, both the stamp and the heading of the Public Security Station are according to procedure. In other words, if a public security station belongs to a centre, for instance, Bijeljina Centre or Banja Luka Centre, it has to put both of those in the heading. So it would say "Public Security Station," and above that it would say "Centre of Security Services."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, could you please tell us, according to this procedure, whose stamp is this?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to the rules and the law and the regulations, this is the Public Security Station stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, that's sufficient. Could we now see document P1409, P1409.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document. My apologies, Your Honours. The tab number is -- perhaps Tanja can find it for us. I believe Ms. Korner used this document, but that they hadn't been listed, so I don't really have that information. Unfortunately, we can only use it as shown on the screen. My apologies. That's on transcript page, and I can say when this was used. That's 23056, 23056 -- 22056.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, as you'll recall, it came up because Mr. Cvijetic was disputing when I was putting to him there was chief of the CSB. And, indeed, as they're not disputing it, I'm at a loss to understand the line of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I just wanted to explain why this may have led to confusion and to doubts about the reliability of this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Orasanin, from this letter of appointment, we can see that Mr. Jesuric was, indeed, appointed as chief of the station.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, this is the only document that can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at the upper left-hand corner. We need to scroll down the Serbian version. We need to see what's above this heading. You can see there that there is something handwritten. Could you please read it out for us? I don't want to give testimony myself.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says: "Sent on the 19th of April, 1992, to Bijeljina."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There we go. In other words, 19 days after the letter of appointment was issued. I see that Mr. Harhoff is warning me that it's time to go on break, so we will break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we rise and resume at 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, whereas we would have taken 10 minutes, nearly, of the time promised to you, we must plead force majeure in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before the witness comes in: At one point, there was a mistake in the transcript, saying that I called His Honour Judge Harhoff "Mr. Harhoff," and I didn't. I would just like to correct that for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm fine with both, Mr. Cvijetic. Don't worry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Either way, I do believe that you're a gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You may call me "sir," then.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a small joke, Your Honour. I just wanted to correct this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, could we shortly move on to document P2017. You see this, Mr. Orasanin? Let's just see the English version as well. This is the appointment of Predrag Jesuric on the 1st of April, and it arrived in Bijeljina on the 19th of April. And now, on the 19th of April, Mr. Jesuric receives a new appointment. Please take a look to what position he was appointed. Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is appointed chief -- head of Personnel Section of the BH MUP. And the date is the 19th of April, 1992, when a previous decision to appoint him arrived in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to make it clear, why there might have been some confusion about his function while you were there. I will show you a next decision, and I would like to ask you to answer briefly, because we have very little time. Could we look at document 1D065615, please. I'll repeat, if necessary. 1D065615.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do we have a tab number?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 39. But to be honest, it's from the Defence binder, tab 39 in the Defence binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Please take a look, Mr. Orasanin. We'll take a quick look. On the 25th of May, 1992, Mr. Stanisic appoints can you see whom? Dragan Devedlaka?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, head of the Bijeljina CSB?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Instead of Mr. Jesuric?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And based on that previous appointment, he was already an employee of the MUP in the Personnel Service. Do you see a small confusion there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at page 2, please. I'll apologise, there is no page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, let me ask you, briefly: Do you know how long Mr. Devedlaka stayed in that function? Just tell me briefly whether you know or you don't know.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know that Mr. Dragan Andan came into that function after him? Did you know that? Tell me that. Did you know that Dragan Andan also came to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and Sinisa Karan.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, I have you recorded on the transcript, on pages 21887, saying that there was nobody at the centre and that you talked to the head of the Legal Affairs. In your opinion, did the Bijeljina CSB function immediately on the 1st of April, when the MUP was established? Did it have all the services, et cetera? Was that your impression during your quick visit? Could you tell me, briefly, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the functional sense. There was some confusion about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Also, let me ask you this: Did you know that Mr. Stanisic made a decision in which the Zvornik SJB was made a part of the Sarajevo CSB? Did you know that it went to the centre; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did this resolve the status of the station in the sense that you mentioned, whether it was Bijeljina or whether it was part of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, it later became a part of Bijeljina, but I can't be precise about the period.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And was it a part of the Sarajevo CSB?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. I just wanted to help, because the question, as translated and as typed, says: "Did this resolve the status of the station in the sense that it was mentioned, whether it was Bijeljina or whether it was part of Zvornik?" Is that what you meant to say? I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was part of the Sarajevo centre when we were there, just as the other stations were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, I have to show you the following document: It's 65 ter, Defence list, 33D1, and now it's 1D571, tab 29. Could we have immediately page 2 in Serbian. Mr. Orasanin, do you remember that you were shown this document by Ms. Korner yesterday in relation to Visegrad? Excuse me, we also need the following page in English, or, more precisely, the page pertaining to Visegrad. Yes. And she was talking about your statement, that war crimes committed against the Serbian population were investigated, and then you said you were referring to just one single crime that had been committed. Now, I don't know where this is in English. We have to go to "Foca." Can we find "Foca" in English, and I would like the same page in Serbian to remain. In Serbian, it's the same page. Mr. Orasanin, you are talking here about record of war criminals. However, you mention "no ethnicity"?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This had to do with the forms, RZ-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, that's all. That's all I needed to show you. The following document is 65 ter 323, or, rather, it's P623 [as interpreted]. P633. And can we have the following page in Serbian, page 2. It's tab 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the last paragraph, sir. I showed you this document, showing that the War Presidency appointed people in the station. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: However, at the bottom of the page, the fourth line from the bottom, it says that there are only five active policemen in the station. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we have the following page in Serbian. That's page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the third paragraph, the big one -- I need the bottom of the third paragraph. We also have to find this in English.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Robbery" and other stuff?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: No, no. I want you to read the part beginning about: "Paramilitary formations are a particularly pronounced problem." Can you find this sentence, where it says: "In these circumstances, the police found itself completely paralysed"? So this is information dating from July. It comes from Visegrad. Does this reflect the realistic picture of the situation in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following document is -- yesterday, you were shown a report on the work of the Ministry of the Interior. P6625 [as interpreted] -- P625. Ms. Korner showed you page 17 in Serbian. In Serbian, can we have page 17. Page 17 in Serbian. Don't zoom in. This is page 30, and we need page 17. In e-court, it's page 21. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now, while they're looking for this part in English, you just read it to yourself in Serbian. The last paragraph on the page: "In this period, crime inspectors ..." In English, it's page 15 in e-court. Do you remember that Ms. Korner showed you this document and asserted that you had the priority in documenting war crimes committed against Serbs? Do you remember that this was mentioned yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you just this: Did you have any intelligence that in the territory controlled by the Muslim forces, war crimes against Serbian population were committed? Merely yes or no will suffice.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The Serbs who had been expelled and fled from this area, were they the ones who informed you about this?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you document their statements?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Let us go back to the previous page in Serbian. It's page 14 in e-court in English. Let me see. One more page in Serbian. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the last paragraph on this page. Let's see if we have it in English. Yes. So take a look at this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Here, we can find the statement about crimes against humanity and international law.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: No ethnicity is mentioned here. It doesn't say anything against whom proceedings should be instituted. It merely says that the proceedings are underway.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, does this comport to your instructions and the forms that you brought into the field?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you just once more. All data that you collected about victims of war crimes, regardless of the ethnicity, are they now being used by the War Crimes Court in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, let us recapitulate. You divided your visits in two categories, visits and instructive supervisions?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: There were four rounds of visits. I don't remember the number of stations that you visited, but I do remember that you visited three centres and a number of stations.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever visit a public security centre in Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there were no communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the blitz visits? And could you give us a "blitz" answer?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I already stated. We simply had to go into the field and get a picture of the situation there. We had to get acquainted with the personnel. They had to inform us about their problems. And later on, we had to find out a solution. So that was the blitz visit. It wasn't an actual inspection.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Were you the first physical contact between the Ministry of the Interior and some of these stations?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was I and Drago Borovcanin. And I'm talking about the places with which we could communicate, where we could actually physically arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: While you were there, did you also perform some tasks that were not necessarily from your jurisdiction? Be brief.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you also take mail? Did you also perform a messenger duty?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did, also personnel duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, after those visits, you should have carried out instructive inspections?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now, objectively speaking about 1992 and the situation in which Republika Srpska found itself at the time, was it possible, with the personnel and equipment that you had, to visit every single public security station and find out what the situation there was?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My following question should be: Was it sometimes the case that you thought that everything was functioning perfectly in a particular station, and when you arrived there, you found out that nothing was functioning there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was our duty, that was the initial assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But did you find out a completely different situation from what you thought you would find there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I already spoke about it. Things were very often quite different from what we thought they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you also visit the towns in and around which battles were fought?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you mention some other town?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, it was also Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And Brcko?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brcko, Foca, Visegrad, Zvornik. All these towns were in the areas where fighting was going on. The roads were not clear. We couldn't arrive to other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My next question: Were you sometimes in a situation where you would enter a city which was completely deserted?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the case both in Foca and in Brcko. It was -- they were ghost towns, as we say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did you have any contacts with paramilitary units, any encounters with them?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I ask how this arises from the cross-examination, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness gave evidence about the situation in Foca, and specifically in Brcko, where he was actually driven away by members of paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I did not challenge any of that. Sorry. I did not challenge any of that, nor did I ask any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, did they threaten you, when you had these encounters with them, or were you provoked by them?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was when --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: No. Just tell us yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, do you have an official ID and a pistol? Have you been issued a pistol, as an authorised officer?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, at the time I did have an old official ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, all I wanted to know was: Were you in a position, you and your colleagues, to actually arrest these men who provoked you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If I may add a short comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, please go ahead. I only have 10 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even have a pistol with me, although that was my duty. But had I had it, it would have actually just provoked them to perhaps shoot us. So we had these situations where we felt like that, and that's the reason why I didn't have the pistol with me, although it is the duty of policemen -- a police officer to carry his weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did any of your colleagues get killed on duty precisely when they had these encounters with paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, there were such cases. It was -- it happened, actually, on this same route which we inspected. There were four police officers who had been killed in Podrinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well, that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's why we were cautious.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I just have two more questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm just going to help you out, Mr. Cvijetic. We do not suggest that the three inspectors should have gone around arresting people. That was not their duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, since you gave evidence about these actions in Zvornik, Foca and so on: Was it possible to actually handle these units in such a way without the special support that you requested, special units and so on?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was impossible without the special police and some other services. And, of course, we also needed technical equipment for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. That's sufficient. Just one last question. Are you aware that Mr. Stanisic had actually ordered that such an operation be conducted in the Trebinje area, in other words, the area where you did not get a chance to go and inspect it; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I said that I took part in preparing the operational plan for that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you were referring to Foca. What I am asking you about is the CSB in Trebinje, and the south-eastern portion. Did you know that there was an operation planned for that area as well?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR ORASANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would have happened after I had already left.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Well, Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Orasanin, we thank you for your attendance before the Tribunal. Your examination is now at an end, and you are now released. And we wish you a safe journey back to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: My recollection is that according to the schedule, we're sitting in afternoons next week. So we take the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just one matter on scheduling. After Your Honours told us yesterday that we would restart the case after the recess on the 29th, it's been brought to our attention that, in fact, the 30th happens to be another UN holiday. I don't know if Your Honours had noticed that one, fixing this, and we simply raise it to see if it would be more sensible to sit on the Wednesday, rather than the Monday. But, I mean, as I say, it's a matter for Your Honours when dealing with the scheduling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I suppose when the calling side would have realised that, we probably could have expected such an application.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, Your Honours -- again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you for bringing that to our attention. No doubt, they would take that on board.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, the only other matter is if we could perhaps know early next week, once we know from Mr. Zecevic about the witnesses, what's going to happen about the Zupljanin case, when it will start, because I think that would help all parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we reconvene on Wednesday afternoon. I wish everyone a safe weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 15th day of June, 2011, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.07 a.m.,
